Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

famished adjective

also starving, ravenous, starved, very hungry

classical

Plaut. Cas. 130: quom lassus fueris et famēlicus
Ter. Eun. 260: ille ubi miser famēlicus videt

famēlicus, famēlica, famēlicum

declension

suffering from hunger, famished, starved

(vōx plērumque cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; posteā Plin., Juv.)

From famēs. Mostly ante- and post-classical, not in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • famēlica hominum nātiō. Quid agitis? ut perītis?

    you starveling tribe of men, how are you? How goes the dying?Plaut. Rud. 311

See also be hungry, hunger, fasting.

SourcesLewis & Short: famelicus

Plautus, Casina 130; Rudens 311. Terence, Eunuchus 260.
